title: Path traversal and archive-entry containment
attackSurface: User-controlled path fragments resolved under a restricted upload root

references.note: Zip Slip archive-entry traversal in plexus-archiver before 3.6.0

hostile.title: Dot-dot slash escape
hostile.why: Classic parent traversal out of an upload root

hostile.title: Nested upload escape
hostile.why: Zip Slip style nested path that escapes after a valid-looking prefix

hostile.title: Backslash traversal
hostile.why: Windows separator form of the same traversal primitive

hostile.title: Percent-encoded traversal
hostile.why: Encoded separator and parent segments that must be decoded before validation

hostile.title: Double-encoded traversal
hostile.why: Nested encoding layer used to bypass one-pass decoding filters

hostile.title: POSIX absolute path
hostile.why: Absolute path replacement instead of containment under the root

hostile.title: Windows drive absolute path
hostile.why: Drive-qualified paths must not become extraction or upload targets

hostile.title: UNC share path
hostile.why: Network share paths can escape both local roots and expected filesystem semantics

benign.title: Current-directory normalization
benign.why: Benign dot segment that remains inside the root

benign.title: Unicode filename
benign.why: Non-ASCII filenames are legitimate user data

benign.title: Spaces in filename
benign.why: Spaces inside a segment are normal on desktop and web uploads

benign.title: Well-known metadata path
benign.why: Leading dot segments can be legitimate when they are not traversal
